subject: general
question: In the rear-view mirror of cars, people use which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror** is used in the rear-view mirrors of cars.
 
• Convex mirrors are chosen because they provide a **wider field of view** compared to flat or concave mirrors.
 
• This wider field of view allows drivers to see more of the area behind them, which helps in preventing accidents.
 
• Convex mirrors also produce **smaller and upright images**, which makes it easier for drivers to judge the distance and speed of vehicles approaching from behind.
 
• These mirrors are also known as **diverging mirrors** because they spread out light rays that strike their surface.
 
• The use of convex mirrors in vehicles is a **safety feature** mandated by many automobile safety regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plano-convex lens**__

 __
 
• A **plano-convex lens** is a type of lens with one flat surface and one convex surface.
 
• These lenses are commonly used in **optical instruments** such as magnifying glasses, cameras, and projectors.
 
• They are not suitable for rear-view mirrors because they do not provide a wide field of view.
 
 
 
• **Concave mirror**__
 __
 
• A **concave mirror** has an inward-curved reflecting surface and is also known as a converging mirror.
 
• These mirrors are used in applications where **focused light** is needed, such as in torches, headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
• Concave mirrors produce a limited field of view, making them unsuitable for use as rear-view mirrors in vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Biconvex lens**__
 
 
• A **biconvex lens** has two outward-curved surfaces.
 
• They are commonly used in **microscopes** and **telescopes** to focus light and form clear images.
 
• Biconvex lenses are not used in rear-view mirrors because they do not offer a wide field of view and can distort the image.
